# Projects Route

*(File kept under its original name, `Projects Route (BpComingSoon)`, so existing links resolve; `BpComingSoon` is now only the fallback this route shows when no project is published.)*

## What `/projects` is on `main`

`app/(site)/projects/page.tsx` builds `views = buildProjectViews(resumeData.projects, resumeData.proofs)` (see [[Career Content]]) and renders a hero ("Selected Work" / "Projects" / "One project — …" or "N projects — …"), then one `<ProjectEntry>` per published project inside `<ProjectListSpine>`, then a `.pj-outro` footer and `<BackToTop />`. Styles come from `app/(site)/projects/projects.css` (`.pj-*`) plus `feature.css` (shared with the About page — see [[About This Site Page]]). When `views` is empty (the Projects switch off in Site Settings, or every project hidden) it falls back to the hero + `<BpComingSoon />` placeholder documented in [[Blueprint UI Components]].

## `components/projects/`

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `ProjectListSpine.tsx` | Client. Wraps the list; a hairline track down the left with an accent fill driven by `useScroll` + `useSpring` (`stiffness 220, damping 34, mass 0.4`). Since 2026-09-20 it is one SVG `<path>` drawn twice (`.pj-spine-track` in `--rule`, `.pj-spine-fill` in `--accent` with framer `pathLength` as the fill) rather than a scaled div, so it can bend: `spinePath()` runs straight down the 2px column and, around every open `.pj-case-study-wrap`, S-curves in (72px of travel) to 12px left of the centred `.pj-case-study` panel's edge, runs alongside it, and S-curves back out just below it into the entry's padding. The path is measured from the DOM into a `useMotionValue` by a `ResizeObserver` on the list (which fires every frame the panel's height animates) plus `resize`, never React state; the excursion scales with the panel's height, so the bend grows and shrinks with the open/close animation. Under 860px the panel is full width, the excursion is under 20px, and the line stays straight. Reduced motion shows it fully drawn (still bent by layout). |
| `ProjectEntry.tsx` | Client. One full-height entry, no pinning: opening hairline rule, a two-column grid (`.pj-entry-text` / `.pj-entry-media`) that alternates sides on odd indexes (`pj-entry--reverse`) and collapses to one column at 860px. Index `01 / 0N`, title, `type`, head rule, summary, bullets (framer variants: `staggerChildren 0.09`, `delayChildren 0.3`), then a "View the full case study" toggle. The media column drifts ±56px against scroll (`useTransform` on a spring; held at 0 in Photo Mode so a drop lands where it looks like it will); an entry with no gallery images renders text-only (`pj-entry--text-only`, no media column), and `useScroll` then gets no target, since a ref that never attaches throws. Since 2026-09-27 the body is rendered block by block — the summary's paragraphs (`splitParagraphs`, each a `p.pj-summary` with `data-pj-block`), then the bullets (each `li` with `data-pj-block`) — so an image with a `place` can leave the grid and float as an `InlinePhoto` at the start of its block (before the `<p>`, since a figure inside one is invalid HTML; inside the `<li>`). "Gallery images" means the ones still unplaced, so with every photo floated the entry goes text-only. Placements live in local state keyed by the image's index (reset when the saved ones change, so the hot-reloaded file takes over after a save); an anchor past the last block falls back to the last (`resolvePlace()` in `lib/photo-place.ts`), and a captured `post` never floats. The entry now owns the `Lightbox`, fed every shown image, so a floated photo and a gallery one page through the same set. |
| `PhotoMode.tsx` | (2026-09-27) Client, dev only. `PhotoModeProvider` wraps the list in `page.tsx` (always a `.pj-photo-scope` div, so the tree doesn't change shape on the client); its toggle (`.pj-photo-dock`, stacked 48px above "Edit in Studio") renders only when `NEXT_PUBLIC_STUDIO_URL` is set and the page is on a loopback host — the same rule as `StudioLink` — and remembers on/off in `sessionStorage`. On, each entry with its own `images` and some body text gets `.is-arranging` (dashed outlines on its body and gallery), gallery shots get a `.pj-photo-grab` layer with a "Place in text" button (block 0, right, 38%), and floated ones get drag, a toolbar and a resize handle (below). `startDrag()` turns a press into a drag after 5px: a ghost (≤280px, clamped to the project's `.bp-shell`) follows the pointer; over the body (24px slack) the target is the `[data-pj-block]` whose top is nearest the ghost's top, the side is whichever half of the body the pointer is in, and a dashed indicator shows the photo's footprint; over the gallery column (or `.pj-photo-return`, which stands in when every photo is floated) it offers "Back to the gallery". Anywhere else — the title, rules, dates, another project — a drop does nothing; Escape cancels; the page auto-scrolls within 72px of the window edge. Saves go one at a time to the Studio's `POST /api/photo-place` (see [[Build Tooling and Config]]); a refusal or an unreachable Studio shows in the status line and puts the saved placement back. |
| `InlinePhoto.tsx` | (2026-09-27) Client. A floated project photo (`figure.pj-inline.pj-inline--left|right`), drawn by the gallery's exported `ShotButton` with `sizes` for its width. Its width is `--pj-inline-w` × `1cqi` — a share of `.pj-body`, which is a size container — so it holds at any screen width. In Photo Mode: a `.pj-photo-grab` layer to drag it; a toolbar (shown on hover/focus) with move up/down a block, float on the other side, and back to the gallery; and a `.pj-photo-resize` handle on the corner facing the text (pull it into the text to grow; `role="slider"`, arrow keys step 2%, Home/End for 15/70%) with a live % readout, saving on release. Arriving from a drop or a step it FLIPs from where it was drawn (WAAPI, 520ms, skipped under reduced motion). | The case study opens via `AnimatePresence` height `0 → auto` (0.55s, the site's `EASE`), and also on its own when the address names the toggle's id, `#project-<id>-case-study` (checked on mount and on `hashchange`; the link a home-page skill linked to a proof uses, see [[Data Layer and Types]]); `.pj-toggle` has `scroll-margin-top: 120px` so that anchor clears the nav; since 2026-09-20 `.pj-case-study` is a centred column (`max-width: 960px; margin-inline: auto`) under the full-width entry, with the spine bending in to run beside it (row above). |
| `ProjectDateBox.tsx` | Client. The optional date box from `project.dates` — see **Dates** below. |
| `ProjectStatus.tsx` | Client component for a project's `status` line. Text fenced in ` ``` ` renders as a monospace code block (`.pj-code`) with a copy-to-clipboard button (lucide `Copy` → `Check` for 1.8s); the rest renders as italic muted text. Used for the Auto App Updater install command. |
| `CaseStudy.tsx` | Server-safe markup for the expanded case study (`ProofView`: eyebrow "Case study", title, subtitle, summary, sections, tags, diagrams). Extracted from `ProjectEntry` so the About page can reuse it. A diagram whose `src` is in `FLOW_DIAGRAMS` renders as `<FlowDiagram>`, and one in `THEMED_SVGS` as `<ThemedSvg>`, instead of an `<img>` (below). |
| `diagrams/ThemedSvg.tsx` | (2026-09-26) Client. For hand-drawn SVG files whose colours and faces are all `var(--token, fallback)`, listed by `src` in `THEMED_SVGS` (`diagrams/themed.ts`, a plain module so `lib/projects.ts` can read it on the server). Renders the file as an `<img>` first (server render, no JS, a failed fetch), then fetches it and inlines the markup so it follows the live palette and `data-theme`; as an `<img>` (the gallery, the Lightbox, the Studio) it can only fall back to the Electric preset by the OS colour scheme. The figure spans the whole assets grid (`.pj-proof-asset--wide`) with no border, since the drawing carries its own hairline frame (`.pj-themed-svg svg` is `width: 100%`). Two in a row are split by a 1px `--faint` rule with padding above the second, the section divider's tone so it reads in both themes. First use: the two UniFi topologies on `unifi-network`, drawn by `scripts/unifi-topology.mjs` (see [[Build Tooling and Config]]). |
| `diagrams/flows.ts` + `diagrams/FlowDiagram.tsx` | (2026-09-20) Flowcharts the site draws inline, keyed by the diagram's `src`: `flows.ts` holds each chart as boxes (`title`, `detail`, `tone: step \| check \| system \| stop`, position in the original 680-wide viewBox) plus edges in pulse order and a legend; `FlowDiagram` (client) lays the arrows out box-edge to box-edge, draws in the palette (`.pj-flow-*` in `projects.css`: neutral steps on `--white`, checks outlined in `--blue`, what lands on the machine filled in `--accent` at 18% with a heavier stroke so the two stay apart in Electric, dead ends dashed and muted) and follows `data-theme`, which an `<img>` SVG cannot. Motion: boxes rise in one every 0.11 s with their arrows drawing (`pathLength`) behind them (`whileInView`, once, the `Reveal` viewport defaults), then a `--accent` dot runs every arrow in turn (0.55 s each) and rests 2.4 s before going round again — one keyframed `motion.circle` per arrow sharing a cycle. `useReducedMotion` renders the finished chart with no dot. The figure spans the assets grid (`.pj-proof-asset--flow`, max 600px) because a 200px column would shrink the labels past reading; when every asset is a flowchart (`.pj-proof-assets--flows`) the grid is `auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 520px), 1fr)`, so two sit side by side once each can have 520px (a desktop case study) and stack below that. The SVG file at `src` stays in `public/` as the Studio thumbnail and the fallback. First use: the two RB's Auto App Updater charts (`/project-artifacts/auto-app-updater/install-flow.svg`, `run-flow.svg`), copied from that repo's `docs/`. |
| `ProjectGallery.tsx` | Client. Since 2026-09-27 it takes optional `items` (which `ShownImage`s to draw — the entry passes only the unplaced ones), `onOpen` (the entry's viewer; without it the gallery keeps its own `Lightbox`, as the About page uses it) and `editing` (Photo Mode's grab and "Place in text"), and exports `ShotButton` (with a `sizes` prop) for `InlinePhoto`. Responsive photo grid (`align-items: start`, since frames can differ in shape); each cell is a fixed-aspect `next/image` frame — 4:3 unless the image's `aspect` picks another ratio, or "original", which drops `fill` for an uncropped `width: 100%; height: auto` image (`.pj-shot-btn--original`) — (`fill`, `sizes` tracking the grid) that uncovers with a `clip-path` wipe (`staggerChildren 0.1`) and opens the `Lightbox`. A `.gif` cell is `unoptimized` (2026-09-20): the optimizer can only pass an animated file through whole, so it is fetched directly and plays at the speed and loop baked into the file by the Studio (see [[Career Content]]). Diagrams from `additionalInfo.assets` stand in when a project has no photos, except `THEMED_SVGS` drawings, which stay in the case study only. An image with `display: "compare"` (2026-09-26) renders as a `CompareImage` instead of a button, with its own corner enlarge control (a slider inside a button would be invalid), and the gallery note adds "drag to compare". An artifact with a `post` (2026-09-27) is drawn by `PostButton` instead of an image frame altogether, and is left out of the "N images · click to enlarge" note under the grid, which counts only the artifacts that actually enlarge. An artifact whose `src` is still empty (a card added in the Studio but not yet given a file) is filtered out before anything renders — `next/image` with `src=""` makes the browser refetch the page itself — and the viewer is handed the same filtered list so the indexes line up. |
| `CompareImage.tsx` | (2026-09-26) Client. A before/after in the image's frame (`--cmp-ratio` from its `aspect`, 4:3 by default and for "original"): the After layered over the Before and uncovered up to a bar (`--cmp-pos`, `clip-path: inset(0 0 0 pos)`). Dragging the frame moves the bar (pointer capture, `touch-action: pan-y` so phones still scroll); a transparent `<input type="range">` over it carries the keyboard and screen-reader path. Each photo either covers the frame (no `frame`) or is placed by its Studio-set `ImageFrame` (left/top/width in % of the frame, height from the image), with `sizes` scaled up by the zoom so a crop isn't soft. Bar, knob and Before/After tags use fixed light colours because they sit on photographs; `.cmp-*` styles in `projects.css`. |
| `Lightbox.tsx` | Client. Full-screen viewer (portal) for the untouched original image, keyboard navigation, loading state. A PDF (2026-09-27) opens as `PdfPages` — every page, scrollable — with the caption tracking the page under the reader ("Page 2 of N", copy key `gallery.pageOf`) and, when the Studio allows it, a `.pj-lb-download` link to the file; `DownloadIcon` is exported from here for the gallery's link too. In the gallery a PDF cell still shows only the saved first-page preview (whole-page shape by default) with a `.pj-shot-tag` ("PDF · N pages") and a `.pj-shot-download` link under the frame, so a page of thumbnails never fetches a PDF. An artifact with a `post` (2026-09-27) renders a `PostCard` under the picture. A comparison shows as a large `CompareImage` (`.pj-lb-compare`, as wide as a 4:3 frame fits in 78vh), and ←/→ leave paging alone while its bar has focus. Because the viewer portals to `<body>`, outside `.bp`, none of the palette tokens reach it — all of its CSS is literal colours, `PostCard` included. |
| `PdfPages.tsx` | (2026-09-27) Client. Every page of a PDF in one scrolling column (`.pj-lb-pdf`), drawn from the file itself by pdf.js. The library and its worker (~1.7MB) sit behind a dynamic `import("pdfjs-dist")`, so only a visitor who opens a PDF fetches them — the projects route's initial JS is unchanged; Turbopack rewrites `new URL("pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.worker.min.mjs", import.meta.url)` to the emitted worker asset. Each page holds its slot from the start (sized by page one's ratio, so the scrollbar is honest before anything is drawn) and rasterises only when it comes near, at the column's width × `devicePixelRatio` capped at 2. A second observer reports the page under the reader so the caption can follow. Pages are drawn on white whatever the theme, as paper is. |
| `PostCard.tsx` | (2026-09-27) Server component, exporting both halves of how a captured post is shown. **`PostButton`** is what the grid gets in place of a thumbnail (`.pj-postcard`): source, author, date, the opening of the post and a "View LinkedIn post" action, sized to its content since the grid aligns cells to the top. A screenshot shrunk into a grid cell is unreadable grey, so the picture is not the invitation. **`PostCard`** is the record in the viewer: the words in the site's type, the sign-off hashtags set apart (`.pj-post-tags`, found by pattern at the end of the text rather than by the line the capture put them on, since the text passes through the Studio's textarea; two or more in a row is the test), "Redirect to LinkedIn", and the date the copy was taken. Only an ISO `date` is reformatted, so a hand-typed "October 2021" is never turned into a day nobody stated. The card uses literal colours (the viewer is portalled outside `.bp`) and is paper with ink in both themes; the grid card uses palette tokens, since the grid is inside `.bp`. At 900px and up the viewer puts the record and the screenshot side by side — record first, larger share — each scrolling on its own, the figure wrapping so the viewer's own caption stays on its own line under both; below that they stack. Fed by `ProjectImage.post`, captured by the Studio — see [[Data Layer and Types]] and [[Career Content]]. |
| `ProjectFeature.tsx` + `feature/*` | The deep-dive used by the About page only — documented in [[About This Site Page]]. |

`lib/projects.ts` (`buildProofView`, `buildProjectViews`) assembles the `ProjectView` each entry consumes (since 2026-09-27 with `ownImages`, true when `images` is the project's own list rather than diagrams standing in, which is what makes a placement saveable).

**Floated photos (2026-09-27).** In `projects.css`, a body with a floated photo (or any body in Photo Mode) becomes `.pj-body--flow`: `display: flow-root` (no float can leave the body, so none can cover the title, the rules or the dates), `container-type: inline-size` (for the `cqi` widths), `max-width: 88ch` with the children's own measures lifted, block spacing by margins equal to the old flex gap (the status line's `+10px` restated, since in flow it would collapse), and `.pj-summary ~ .pj-summary` spacing so a figure between two paragraphs doesn't break blueprint.css's `p + p`. Its bullets drop the outside `::marker` for an inline accent dot hung 20px left of the line it starts (an outside marker would stay at the list's edge, on the far side of a left photo). Floats are `clear`ed per side and keep a side margin wider than that dot. At 640px and under photos stop floating and take the full width — before their paragraph, or under a bullet's words. `lib/photo-place.ts` holds the rules both sides use: `PLACE_WIDTH` (15–70%, 38% to start, 2% keyboard step), `ShownImage`, `clampWidth()`, `resolvePlace()`, `canFloat()`.

`EmphasizedText` (`components/content/`) renders the bullets' `emphasis` phrases, which take the accent on hover; `EmphasizedText` (`components/content/`) renders the bullets' `emphasis` phrases, which take the accent on hover. Each entry is `id="project-<id>"`, the anchor the resume's inline evidence links (`/projects#project-icarus-lite`) jump to. `<BackToTop />` now comes from `components/blueprint/` (moved 2026-09-15).

## What is published

One project since 2026-09-16: **ICARUS-Lite** (`order: 1`) — six photographs from `public/project-images/ICARUS-Lite/` in its gallery (the earlier duplicate render pair is gone), a `status` line under the summary ("Project page under development. More details to come soon."), and a case study built from its `additionalInfo` (its diagram `assets` were dropped, so the gallery is photos only). The other eight projects are `visible: false` drafts in the Studio ("1 on the site · 8 drafts") and never reach `resumeData.projects`. All 17 entries in `proofs.json` are also `visible: false`, so `buildProofView` currently sees no proof for any project and the case study is the project's own write-up — see [[Career Content]].

## Dates

Every project can carry a `dates` object (`types/resume.ts` → `ProjectDates`; Studio → Projects → **Dates**): `start`, optional `end`, `ongoing`, `position`. ISO dates (`2026-06-28`) are formatted by `lib/dates.ts` (`Jun 28, 2026`); anything else shows as written. When `start` is set, `ProjectEntry` renders `<ProjectDateBox>`:

- **Position** `top-right` (default) / `top-left` — the box sits *on* the entry's opening hairline rule (`.pj-entry-rule { position: relative }`, box absolutely centered on the line with paper behind it, so the rule reads as passing through a tag). `bottom-right` / `bottom-left` — the same on a closing rule rendered after the grid. `inline` — in the text column under the head rule. Under 860px the corner positions drop into the flow above the grid.
- **Ongoing** — the end reads "→ Present" (accent) and the box's 2px underline becomes an indeterminate progress bar: `pj-dates-fill` scales to 92% over 1.6s on view (`useInViewOnce`), then `pj-dates-chase` sweeps a lighter band across it every 2.8s. Static projects show a hairline underline. Reduced motion snaps the fill and runs the sweep once, off-track.

No published project sets `dates` yet; the About page's hero uses the same component at `size="large"`.

## History

The pre-reskin `/projects` route (`Version-2.0`) rendered `ProjectsExplorer` / `ProjectDetails` (a carousel, a lightbox, and a right-side `AdditionalInfoDrawer`); the reskin replaced it with the `BpComingSoon` placeholder, and the Sep 12–13 rebuild (`72823d7`, `c5f1f19`, `32a51c7`) produced the current editorial flow — deliberately with no pinning or scroll-jacking. The abstract SVGs in `public/project-artifacts/` are the diagram fallbacks `ProjectGallery` shows for projects without photos.
